title: Trying out the new Customer Conversation harness in Copilot Studio
bodyHtml:
Microsoft released a new option in Copilot Studio called the Customer Conversation harness. It is in public preview. I have not built anything with it yet, so this post is me checking out what it is first, and then setting up a small agent to try it. If you want to follow along, the steps and prompts are below.

What is a harness?

Copilot Studio now lets you choose how an agent works when you create it. Microsoft calls these choices harnesses. The Harnesses in Copilot Studio page lists three:

  • Standard is the rule-based agent and agent flow style most of us already know.
  • GitHub Copilot is for multi-step reasoning work, like creating and editing Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF files. Despite the name, it is a Copilot Studio framework and not the GitHub Copilot service.
  • Customer Conversation is the new one. It is for customer-facing agents that talk over voice or chat.

What is Customer Conversation?

These agents answer in natural conversation instead of following a fixed script. An agent is made of a main agent plus sub-agents, and each sub-agent can hand the conversation to a human. Microsoft calls them Customer Assist Agents.

You publish them in two ways: as chat on a website, or on a phone number for calls. 

What the build screen looks like

From the docs, an agent has five tabs: Build, Preview, Evaluate, Deploy and Monitor. On Build you get:

  • Instructions, with one tab for Speech and one for Chat.
  • Knowledge, where you add sources like a website.
  • Tools and skills, which can be connectors, MCP servers, workflows, AI Builder prompts and REST APIs (preview).
  • Sub-agents and connected agents.
  • Events: Conversation Start, End of Conversation and On Error.

Two built-in tools are listed. Escalate passes the conversation to Teams Phone, email, or a live agent. Biometric Authentication checks who is calling, and the docs put it under Voice capabilities in the agent configuration panel, not under Tools.

A few things to know before you start

  • It runs on Copilot Credits, and building, testing and evaluating can use credits too.
  • Speech does not support end-user sign-in, so a knowledge source that needs a login only works in chat.
  • It is preview, so screens and settings can change.

Let's try it

I am using this blog  as the knowledge source. It covers Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry and AI Builder, and I know the content well enough to tell if the agent gets something wrong. Swap in your own site if you follow along.

Step 1: Create the agent

On the Copilot Studio home page, open Explore what else is possible with agents and pick the Customer Conversation tile. You can also go to Agents, then New agent, and look for the Customer Conversation badge.


Step 2: Describe the agent

Choose to describe the agent instead of starting blank, adjust this prompt to your fit and paste:

Create a customer-facing agent called "decuba.tech Guide". It answers questions from readers of the decuba.tech blog about Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry and AI Builder. It helps beginners and intermediate users find the right article, explains concepts in plain language, and points to the matching post on https://decuba.tech. It only answers from the blog content. If the blog does not cover a question, it says so and suggests the closest article. It can speak (phone) and chat (website).

Select Generate.Wait till the creation is finished

Step 3: Knowledge source

On Build, open Knowledge, the website  https://decuba.tech is already addes from the description. A public site should work for both chat and voice, so it is a simple place to start.

Step 4: Write the instructions

On Build, open Instructions. Paste this into the Chat tab:

You are the decuba.tech Guide, a chat assistant for readers of https://decuba.tech.

Scope: Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry and AI Builder, as covered on the blog.

Rules:
- Answer only from the decuba.tech knowledge source. Never invent steps, menu names or limits.
- When a post covers the question, give a short answer (up to 5 sentences), then name the post and link it as https://decuba.tech/posts/<slug>.
- If the blog has no post on the topic, say "I could not find that on decuba.tech" and offer the closest related post.
- For step-by-step questions, use a numbered list of no more than 7 steps.
- Write in plain, direct language for beginners and intermediate users. No marketing wording.
- If the reader asks for a person, or the question is about hiring, consulting or anything outside the blog, use the Escalate tool.

Then paste this into the Speech tab. It is shorter because a caller cannot scan a link:

You are the decuba.tech Guide, a phone assistant for readers of the decuba.tech blog.

Rules:
- Answer only from the decuba.tech knowledge source. Never guess.
- Keep every answer to 3 short sentences. Say one idea at a time.
- Do not read out URLs. Say the post title and tell the caller it is on decuba.tech.
- Do not read lists longer than 3 items. Offer to go through the rest step by step.
- If you did not catch the question, ask the caller to repeat it once.
- If the blog does not cover the question, say so, and name the closest topic.
- If the caller asks for a person, or the question is outside the blog, use the Escalate tool.

[SCREENSHOT: Instructions area with Speech and Chat tabs]

Step 5: Add Escalate

Under Tools and skills, add the Escalate tool and point the email option at an address you check. Then open Preview and paste:

I'd like to talk to a person about a consulting project.

[SCREENSHOT: Escalate triggered in Preview]

Step 6: Ask it some questions

In Preview, try questions based on my recent posts:

How do I build an autonomous agent in Copilot Studio?

Can I connect Codex to a Copilot Studio agent with MCP?

Where do I find my AI Builder credits?

How do I get around the new Microsoft Foundry portal?

Then one the blog does not cover, to see what the agent does:

What does Microsoft Teams Premium cost per user?

I am hoping for "I could not find that on decuba.tech" and a related post. Afterward, run the same five questions in Evaluate and look at how many Copilot Credits it used.

Step 7: Publish

From Deploy, publish to the demo website. If you have a phone number available, try one call.

[SCREENSHOT: Deploy tab with Speech and Chat channels]

I am leaving Biometric Authentication, web search and the contact center connection for later. Each one needs its own setup and licensing, so they make more sense as a second round.

Next

Once the agent is running, I will write up what happened in each step: how the Speech and Chat instructions behaved, what Escalate did, and how many credits the test cost. If you try it first, I would like to hear how it wen
